hero.title: Constituents of Laser
hero.lead: Three fundamental components must be present in every laser device: the active medium, in which population inversion is achieved; the resonator, which amplifies light through repeated reflections; and the pumping technique, which supplies the active medium with the energy needed for excitation.

objectives: Define the active medium and explain its role in achieving population inversion.
Explain the structure of the resonator and the mechanism of amplifying light through repeated reflections between the two mirrors.
List the three types of pumping technique and distinguish between them.

content.caption: Figure 6-11: Diagram of the components of a laser device — the active medium between two mirrors, with the energy source (pumping technique) below it

content.label: 📌 1- Active Medium Active Medium
content.html: This is a collection of atoms, molecules, or ions in a (solid, liquid, or gaseous) state, in which population inversion can be achieved by supplying the active medium with the intensity needed to excite it.

content.label: 📌 2- Resonator Resonator
content.html: This is a suitably designed chamber consisting of two mirrors, with the active material placed between them. The two mirrors are designed to face each other, one being fully reflective and the other partially reflective. See Figure 6-12.

content.caption: Figure 6-12: The resonator — the active medium between a fully reflective mirror and a partially reflective one, from which the laser beam exits

content.html: So the beam incident on one mirror reflects parallel to the main axis of the two mirrors, then strikes the other mirror and reflects from it, and so the reflections of the beam succeed one another inside the resonator. The number of photons generated by stimulated emission thus increases, and after the amplification process reaches an enormous number, the partially reflective mirror allows a fraction of the light incident on it to pass out of the resonator, while reflecting the rest of the light back inside the resonator to sustain the amplification process.

content.label: 📌 3- Pumping Pumping
content.html: This is the technique responsible for supplying the atoms of the active medium with the energy needed to excite them and move them from the stable level to the excited level, achieving the state of population inversion and generating laser light.

content.label: 🔢 List — The three types of pumping technique
content.html:
🔢 List — The three types of pumping technique
  1. 1- Optical Pumping Optical Pumping.
  2. 2- Electrical Pumping Electrical Pumping.
  3. 3- Chemical Pumping Chemical Pumping.

questions.question: The collection of atoms, molecules, or ions in which population inversion is achieved is called:
questions.explain: The active medium is the collection of atoms, molecules, or ions in which population inversion can occur.

questions.question: In the resonator, one mirror is fully reflective and the other is:
questions.explain: One of the resonator's mirrors is designed to be fully reflective, and the other partially reflective, to allow the laser beam to pass through it.

questions.question: The technique responsible for moving atoms of the active medium from the stable level to the excited level is called:
questions.explain: The pumping technique is responsible for supplying the atoms of the active medium with the energy needed to move them from the stable level to the excited level.

questions.question: The three types of pumping technique are:
questions.explain: The three types of pumping technique are: optical pumping, electrical pumping, and chemical pumping.

summary.heading: 📋 Lesson Summary
items: The active medium: atoms, molecules, or ions (solid/liquid/gaseous) in which population inversion is achieved.

The resonator: two facing mirrors (one fully reflective, the other partial) that amplify light through repeated reflections, with part of the beam exiting through the partial mirror as the laser beam.
The pumping technique: supplies the active medium with the energy needed for excitation; its three types are optical, electrical, and chemical.
